commits.message:
[NVIDIA] Build host maps for 64-value FP6 TMA stores on SM103 (#12614)

On GB300 (SM103), Triton and Gluon can use a host tensor descriptor with
an unswizzled 2D box of `[M, 64]` to store FP6. Each row contains 64
byte lanes in `b6p2x16` shared memory. TMA compacts them to 48 bytes in
global memory. The same descriptor is passed by value to every CTA.

The CUDA driver encoder requires an inner box of 128 FP6 values. SM103
also accepts 64 for stores. The tiled host encoder recognizes that case
from the CUDA element type and physical box width and fills the
descriptor directly. Its opaque field encoding was determined on GB300.
[SM103 store restrictions in PTX ISA
9.2](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/archive/13.2.0/parallel-thread-execution/index.html#data-movement-and-conversion-instructions-tensor-copy-restrictions)
· [CUDA tensor-map
encoder](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TENSOR__MEMORY.html)

The compiler checks that each narrow host descriptor is used directly by
tiled TMA stores. The NVIDIA store lowering checks the target, and the
launcher checks the device and the fields it encodes. A hardware box can
cover 1 through 256 rows.

Tests compare E2M3 and E3M2 stores with a software packer, including row
pitches of 48 and 112 bytes, column offsets of 0 and 64 values, guard
bytes, and two CTAs sharing a descriptor. Negative tests cover an SM100
store, an SM103 load, and a descriptor passed through a non-inlined
call.

commits.message:
[Gluon] Fold uniform comparisons of tt.make_range (#12636)

Fold a comparison against a constant when every element in the range
agrees. This removes a full-tile mask before memory-width selection
while preserving the partial tail.

In a 513-column two-tile softmax on GB300, five scalar loads and five
scalar stores became one 128-bit access and one guarded 32-bit access in
each direction. Runtime went from 4.872 to 3.791 µs (22% less time), and
from 6.074 to 4.820 µs at 767 columns (21%).

Folding a mask can also expose a wide byte store. `packLLVector` now
builds 32-bit groups of narrow lanes and joins them with typed LLVM
shuffles, preserving lane order and allowing the backend to reuse packed
conversion results. On GB300, a Gluon FP32-to-E4M3 conversion storing
eight bytes per thread drops from six `PRMT` instructions to zero and
emits one `STG.E.64`. The tests cover 16-bit lane packing and FP8 stores
on SM90 and SM100.

commits.message:
[GPU] Omit redundant memory predicates in elected-thread scopes (#12638)

Inside an elected-thread scope, return only the residual CTA predicate.
Use same-width integer bits for floating operands of integer atomic RMWs
so scalar and tensor bitwise atomics can take the unconditional LLVM
path.

On GB300, row moments went from two `STG.E` to one `STG.E.64` and from
12 to 10 registers. Median kernel time was 5.067 µs before and 5.074 µs
after (neutral).

affected_interfaces: lib/Dialect/Triton/IR/Ops.cpp::AtomicRMWOp::verify (shared C++ TTIR verifier added by the commit)
deep_analysis.adaptation_guide: This commit has three parts: (1) emitMemoryThreadPredicate change in lib/Conversion/TritonGPUToLLVM/Utility.cpp + Utility.h — this is the NVIDIA GPU->LLVM path that triton-ascend does NOT use, so no action. (2) A new AtomicRMWOp::verify() in lib/Dialect/Triton/IR/Ops.cpp with 'let hasVerifier = 1' on TT_AtomicRMWOp in TritonOps.td, rejecting AND/OR/XOR atomic RMW when the element type is not integer. This verifier lives in the shared platform-independent Triton (TTIR) dialect that Ascend consumes, so after syncing upstream it will be enforced in Ascend's TritonToLinalg path. (3) A frontend refactor in python/triton/language/semantic.py that routes atomic_and/or/xor through a new _atomic_bitwise() helper which bitcasts floating operands to same-width integers before emitting the RMW and bitcasts the result back. triton-ascend vendors its OWN fork of python/triton/language/semantic.py whose atomic_and/or/xor (lines ~1435-1454) still emit tt.atomic_rmw AND/OR/XOR directly on the original (possibly float) value, and whose atom_red_typechecking_impl does not reject f32/f64 for bitwise atomics. Net effect: if Ascend syncs this commit without porting the frontend change, tl.atomic_and/or/xor on a float pointer will produce tt.atomic_rmw on a float element and fail the new verifier ('and/or/xor requires an integer element type'). Required adaptation in third_party/ascend's forked semantic.py: port the upstream _atomic_bitwise() helper and rewrite atomic_and/or/xor to call it (bitcast ptr to tl.pointer_type(tl.get_int_dtype(dtype.primitive_bitwidth, signed=False), ptr.type.scalar.address_space), bitcast val to the int dtype, emit the RMW, then bitcast the old value back to the original dtype). Note two fork-specific details: Ascend's pointer_type uses an int address_space (default 1) rather than upstream's string 'global', and its builder method is self.tensor(...) not self.make_tensor(...); use ptr.type.scalar.address_space as upstream does so it is correct under both conventions. Alternatively, if Ascend does not intend to support float bitwise atomics, add an explicit rejection of non-integer element types for and/or/xor in atom_red_typechecking_impl to produce a clean Python-level error instead of an IR verification failure. The C++ verifier itself needs no Ascend-side change (it is inherited from upstream's shared Triton dialect).

[NVIDIA] Reuse shuffle-up bounds predicates in full-warp scans (#12642)

commits.message:
[NVIDIA] Add padded FP6 conversion and compacting TMA stores to Triton (#12541)

Regular Triton kernels can convert floating-point values to FP6 and
store them with TMA on SM100 and SM103. **The TMA box is 128 values wide
on both targets**, so each row writes 96 packed bytes to global memory.

`triton.language.extra.cuda.to_fp6` accepts FP32, FP16, or BF16 and
rounds to E2M3 or E3M2 using round-to-nearest-even with finite
saturation. It returns a `uint8` tile with one FP6 code in the low six
bits of each byte. The store stages those bytes in the `b6p2x16`
shared-memory layout from #12548, and TMA packs them on the way to
global memory.

Use block shape `[BLOCK_M, 128]` to store `BLOCK_M` rows per program.
This example builds a host descriptor for a one-row store into a
contiguous `uint8` destination with 96 bytes per row.

```python
from triton.tools.tensor_descriptor import TensorDescriptor

desc = TensorDescriptor.from_tensor(packed, [1, 128], fp6_format="e2m3")
```

One program can then convert and store one contiguous input row.

```python
import triton
import triton.language as tl
from triton.language.extra.cuda import to_fp6

@triton.jit
def store_fp6_row(src, desc):
    row = tl.program_id(0)
    x = tl.load(src + row * 128 + tl.arange(0, 128))
    desc.store([row, 0], to_fp6(x, "e2m3")[None, :])
```

Kernels can also build the descriptor with
`tl.make_tensor_descriptor(..., fp6_format="e2m3")`. The inner extent
and column offset count FP6 values. Outer strides count bytes.

GB300 tests compare the converted codes and the packed destination byte
for byte for `BLOCK_M = 1, 2, 16, 128, 256`, both FP6 formats, all three
input dtypes, and host- and device-built descriptors. They also check
rounding at a tie and a store at column 128. Both descriptor paths
cross-compile for SM100.

The separate follow-up #12614 adds 64-value host stores on GB300.

commits.comment: [NVIDIA] 当循环内 tmem_read 与 useAcc=False 不一致时禁用 tmem 多缓冲。MMAv5PipelineUtility.cpp 新增 inferNextAccOnRead 递归推断 tmem_read 路径上 nextUseAcc 的值（支持常量、enclosing if、select、if 结果），accReadsForceBufferSwitch 要求每个 in-loop tmem read 都蕴含 nextUseAcc==false；accOverwrittenInLoop 收紧为同 block 且谓词恒为真的 TMEMStoreOp；isAccMultibufferingPossible 改为 (accReadsForceBufferSwitch && accUseFlagSetToFalse) || accOverwrittenInLoop。测试新增周期 reset、select reset、predicated reset store 等场景。NVIDIA Blackwell tmem 多缓冲优化逻辑。
commits.message:
[NVIDIA] Disable tmem multi-buffer if there are inconsistent tmem_read and useAcc=False in the loop (#12562)

We will only allow tmem multi-buffer when every in-loop tmem read
implies nextUseAcc == false: switching to a new accumulator

commits.comment: [ConSan] 在启动屏障前初始化全部状态。Utility.cpp 的 populateAndPassToWarpSpecialize 将 lock 变量分配、CTA0 lock release 与启动屏障从 commit tensor 创建之前移到所有状态（commit tables 等）创建之后，确保其他 CTA 通过屏障时 CTA0 已填满所有共享集群状态，避免 false race 或掩盖真实 race；新增 NV/AMD 两个 lit 测试验证 fill_global_tensor 先于 lock_release 与 barrier。ConSan 属于 experimental/gsan 相关插桩，Ascend 参考架构中 gsan 使用与否未明确，但该文件为 lib/Dialect/TritonInstrument，非 Ascend 核心路径。
commits.message:
[ConSan] Initialize all state before the startup barrier (#12333)

Move lock initialization and startup synchronization after all sanitizer
state initialization. Previously, the commit tables were zero-filled
after the startup barrier, so another CTA could read them before CTA0
initialized them, or have its updates overwritten by CTA0. This could
cause false race reports or hide real races.
